title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from neighbouring pages: Grothendieck is setting up a combinatorial or PL calculus of plane 'figures' inside a closed polygonal domain I with boundary ∂I. The figure is written as underlined L on p.14, as a script letter (Φ on p.16) here; the machine transcription's 𝔊 and 𝔓 are almost certainly the same handwritten Φ, or Φ and an auxiliary figure. Each figure Φ has a finite set of vertices δΦ. ∂Φ is the set of 'boundary vertices' (sommets-bord), those lying on ∂I. There is a duality Φ ↦ Φ*. Φ** is a 'purification' of Φ: next page has Purif(M) and the bijection Φ ↦ Omb°(Φ) onto constructible parts. The order ord(s,Φ) ∈ {0,1,2} classifies vertices.

The page first records doubts about the usefulness of the boundary vertices, since ∂Φ = ∂Φ* holds essentially. A crossed-out attempt splits ∂Φ and ∂Φ* into a common part plus a part on ∂I. He then states the duality behaviour of the vertex types:
(i) Φ_is = Φ*_lac and Φ_lac = Φ*_is: isolated and lacunary vertices are exchanged by duality.
(ii) Φ_red = δΦ \ (δΦ ∩ δΦ*), the vertices not seen by the dual. This splits as the disjoint union of (δΦ \ δΦ**), the 'evanescent' vertices killed by purification, and the 'redundant' vertices proper lying on ∂I.
(iii) The NB gives Φ*_red as the part of ∂I not met by the vertex set.
(iv) ∂*Φ = ∂*Φ*, where ∂*Φ = ∂Φ \ (∂Φ ∩ ∂I) is the set of non-exterior boundary vertices.

Hence, in the canonical decomposition δΦ = Φ_red ∪ Φ_is ∪ Φ_lac ∪ ∂*Φ:
- the 2nd and 3rd terms are swapped by duality;
- the boundary term is self-dual;
- the first term disappears under duality, but its part Φ_red ∩ ∂I reappears under biduality.

He then rethinks the terminology. Since 'redundant' is inadequate, he calls Φ_év the evanescent vertices and proposes 'semi-evanescent' for the old redundant ones. This leads (next page) to an extended vertex set δ̂Φ = δΦ ∪ ∂I. Its six-term decomposition is better adapted to duality and serves to prove cons-W°(Φ) = Omb°(Φ*) and the bijection Purif(M) → Cons(M). The page is purely bookkeeping of how vertex strata behave under a duality/purification operation on PL constructible figures.
errors: 'le troisième est invariant par dualité' should refer to the fourth term ∂*Φ; the third term (Φ_lac) is exchanged with the second.

The first formula Φ_red = δΦ \ δΦ∩δΦ* and the NB formula Φ*_red = ∂I \ (∂I∩∂Φ) are not obviously consistent as written. The page itself shows the definition of 'redundant' being revised; on p.16 this becomes Φ_séc = ∂I \ ∂I∩δΦ*.
∂Φ = ∂Φ* is asserted only loosely ('coïncide ... ?'). The crossed-out lines show it holds only after removing points of ∂I, i.e. as ∂*Φ = ∂*Φ*.

ideas.what: Classification of the vertices of a plane PL figure (isolated, lacunary, redundant/evanescent, boundary) and their behaviour under a duality Φ↦Φ* with Φ** a purification
ideas.modern_name: stratification/vertex bookkeeping for a duality on PL constructible sets (loosely akin to duality of constructible sets/functions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no specific attribution; constructible-function dualities in Euler calculus are due to Schapira, Viro and Kashiwara–Schapira (~1988–91)

ideas.what: Terminology 'sommets évanescents' (δΦ \ δΦ**) vs 'semi-évanescents', with the exchange is ↔ lac and self-duality of non-exterior boundary vertices

missed.claim: A possible (speculative) link exists between the duality on plane figures (lacunary ↔ isolated vertices, bidual = purification, used to show Purif(M) ≅ Cons(M) on the next page) and later dualities on constructible sets/functions (Verdier-type duality in Euler calculus). This page is only bookkeeping and does not itself make the link.
missed.quote: les 2e et 3e termes s'échangent par dualité, le troisième est invariant par dualité, le premier disparaît par dualité - mais ... réapparaît par bidualité
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal: it might show Grothendieck working on a tame/PL constructible-set duality in 1986, in the spirit of the 'tame topology' programme of the Esquisse. The content of this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine combinatorial bookkeeping and terminology revision for vertex types under a duality on plane figures. The main interest is historical: it documents 1986 work on PL constructible figures. No new result appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: The script letters transcribed as 𝔊 and 𝔓 are most likely the same handwritten Φ (underlined L on the previous page, Φ on the next). '∂𝔓∩∂I' should probably read '∂Φ∩∂I'.
'Du coup, l'intérêt de l'introduction des ∂𝔊 dur' — 'dur' is probably 'des' or part of '∂Φ (des sommets-bord de Φ)'.
'ald' probably stands for 'au lieu de' (instead of).
'le troisième [?] est invariant' — the handwriting may read 'le quatrième'; mathematically it must be the fourth term ∂*Φ.
'[-supposés-] lacunaires et isolés' — the crossed word appears to be 'sommets'; the line reads 'sommets lacunaires et isolés de Φ et de Φ* s'échangent'.
